title: Fruit and Shoot borer on African Eggplant

Header: Fruit and Shoot borer on African Eggplant

Prevention: Promptly remove and destroy infested shoots and fruit at regular intervals until final harvest
Promptly eliminate eggplant stubble from old plantings to prevent movement or carryover to new crop or from season to season
Monitoring: Monitor frequently and look for holes made near the growing point or into the flower buds or fruits.
The feeding habit of the larvae may cause the wilting of young shoots, followed by drying and drop-off.
Damaged fruit exhibits holes on the surface, which often are sealed with excreta.
When cut, tunnels created by the larvae are filled with faecal pellets.
The larvae are pink with sparse hairs on the warts on the body and a dark brown or blackish head.
The adult moth is white or dirty white with pale brown or black spots on the thorax and abdomen.
